Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware - AOL Skip to main content Advertisement San Anto..., TX San Antonio, TX Local News Menu 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Sign in Mail 24/7 Help For premium support please call: Missouri State's injury report entering CUSA game against Delaware Liam Keating, Springfield News-Leader Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:11 PM UTC 0 SPRINGFIELD — There’s little time to dwell and celebrate Missouri State’s win over Kennesaw State on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The Bears (2-4, 1-1 in CUSA) are moving on to its next Conference USA clash against Delaware (2-4, 0-2) on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Against the Owls, Missouri State was without three key players on the offensive side of the ball. Missouri State was down three starters in running back Breezy Dubar, offensive lineman Ryan Mitchell and wide receiver Mekhi Miller. “Two guys are concussion guys that I expect we get back this week being Breezy and Ryan,” Woods said. Missouri State: Casey Woods pushes for more Group of Six representation in expanded CFP Missouri State: Jmariyae Robinson one step closer to the triple crown As for Miller, the fifth-year player suffered an injury during pregame warmups against Kennesaw State. Woods does not know the extent of the injury as of Thursday, Oct. 15. “Mekhi had a weird thing come up pregame,” Woods said. “We are still doing some more. I don’t have enough information to get you exactly what’s going on with that right now.” Dubar has rushed for 218 yards, which ranks second-best on the team. He’s also tied with Ramone Green Jr. with two touchdowns for the most on the roster. Mitchell featured on the offensive line in every game before missing the last game. Miller is Missouri State’s third-best wide receiver option. He has 13 catches for 146 yards. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. The No. 5 Hoosiers play host to the fourth-ranked Buckeyes with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to the Big Ten Championshiop Game in Indianapolis The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). picks.headline: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7?
picks.blurb: Ohio State On SI Staff Picks: Can Buckeyes Get Revenge on Indiana in Week 7? Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB This game needs no introduction. Some may argue this is the game Ohio State has been preparing fo r all season long . Now it has a chance to go to Indiana and rewrite a wrong from last December, when it lost the Big Ten Championship game to the Hoosiers, which ultimately led to them completing their undefeated season. Ohio State isn’t undefeated like Indiana is. However, the Buckeyes are rolling through the start of the Big Ten schedule without any real hiccups. Ohio State (5-1, 3-0 Big Ten) has had this game against the Hoosiers (6-0, 3-0 Big Ten) earmarked on the schedule since it was released. So much so that both teams have remained the class of the Big Ten all year long, with a possible elimination scenario in play come December, ahead of the Big Ten title game in Indianapolis. Someone’s supremacy must be disrupted . Will the Buckeyes struggle again, or will the Hoosiers exploit their weaknesses? Check out our staff picks as the game gets underway. Ohio State vs. Indiana Week 7 Outlook Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day watches during the NCAA football game against the Maryland Terrapins at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: noon ET/9 a.m. PT TV Channel: FOX (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -3; over/under is 50.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, Ind. Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 87-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Indiana: A 13-10 loss in the Big Ten title game in a top-two showdown. Ohio State leads the series dating back to 1989, 31-1-1. Pregame festivities: Big Noon Kickoff will be there. Ohio State so far this season: 5-1 (3-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando: 6-0 Dylan Buganski : 5-1 Rafael Zamorano : 4-1 (no pick in Week 6 nor Week 7) Chip Minnich : 4-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 28, Indiana 24 There is no such thing as a one-game season, but the Buckeyes may beg to differ. Indiana handed Ohio State one of its two back-to-back losses to end last season and now, on a fall Saturday in Bloomington, the entire year could come down to whether Ohio State can finally sneak up and regain head-to-head dominance and steal a road win. If wideout Jeremiah Smith gets space and gets comfortable thanks to Julian Sayin, and forces the defense to tire Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, the game could easily deliver a fantastic finish in the closing minutes. We’ll see if the Buckeyes can make it interesting, or better yet, secure a road win that could change the season for good. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Indiana 28 The highly anticipated, top-five Big Ten showdown between the Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday hinges on how Ryan Day's squad handles sudden depth issues against an elite Indiana defense. Ohio State faces an uphill battle following a troubling availability report ruling out two of the team's most relied-upon members on offense ~ Austin Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson. With Austin Siereveld missing his second straight game, the loss of the Preseason All-Big Ten selection strips the Buckeyes of their offensive line leader. This forces Gabe VanSickle and right tackle Phillip Daniels into hyper-extended roles against a vicious Hoosier pass rush; Daniels has not played since the loss at Texas on September 12th. Ja'Kobi Jackson, the team's powerhouse short-yardage back and touchdown leader (6 TDs), is sidelined with a surprise ankle injury. While Bo Jackson will shoulder the primary workload, Ja'Kobi Jackson's absence eliminates the physical lightning-and-thunder dynamic Ohio State uses to control the tempo. Could Isaiah West, who missed a key block that led to a pick-six interception in last week's Maryland game, get a chance at redemption? West offers a physical style of play comparable to Ja'Kobi Jackson. The fans who have been clamoring for Legend Bey may see Bey as a larger part of the offensive game plan. Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith will need to be creative in the run game and involve other receiving talents beyond Jeremiah Smith. With a depleted ground game and a reshuffled protection unit, the entire game plan in my estimation rests on the shoulders of junior quarterback Julian Sayin. Sayin has been using his legs to gain positive yardage in recent games and may need to run more frequently than desired by Sayin or the Ohio State coaching staff. The Ohio State defense is going to be tested, as Indiana boasts talented wide receivers in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker, plus a strong running game led by Turbo Richard. Quarterback Josh Hoover has not yet thrown an interception this season, so perhaps Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia will be able to scheme some situations that result in a turnover. Expect a classic, physical Big Ten chess match. While Indiana enters the match healthier and with a strong defensive front, Sayin's elite talent and postseason poise will provide just enough explosive plays in a late two-minute drill to secure a tight, field-goal victory for the Buckeyes in Bloomington. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Indiana 17 There may not be a matchup this team as well as fans circled coming into this season then the rematch of last year’s Big Ten Championship game in what may be Indiana’s biggest home game in program history. There are old and new faces on both sides, and the clash between head coaches Ryan Day and Curt Cignetti may become one of the conference’s greatest rivalries going forward. Ohio State comes into this matchup battle-tested, seeing ranked teams Iowa and Texas on the road and finishing 1-1 in those matchups. This will be Indiana’s first ranked matchup of the season, but they had a comeback victory at Nebraska last week, in which the Cornhuskers should probably have been a ranked team. This matchup will come down to how dominant Indiana can be at the line of scrimmage, as that may be the only position where Indiana may have more talent than the Buckeyes, other than maybe running back. Indiana should be able to run the ball decently and stop the run on the other side. At the end of the day, the secondary for Ohio State should limit the passing game from exploding and another weapon in the passing game has a big game next to Smith, inching Ohio State to a win in this matchup and moving what we may call in 10 years the “Cignetti-Day War” to a 2-1 Buckeye lead. away.blurb: That’s when Timmons stepped in. The Pennsylvania native punched the ball out before Chandler hit the turf. Ohio State recovered the fumble, ending an Indiana drive during the middle eight minutes of the game. That sequence from Timmons proved to be pivotal, with Ohio State’s offense mustering only 19 points on a day when quarterback Julian Sayin struggled before suffering a right-arm injury that’ll keep him out “several weeks,” per coach Ryan Day . The unit’s momentum carried into the win at Indiana, with Timmons playing a key role in his return. However, he couldn’t finish the contest. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Jay Timmons was an under-the-radar champion of the Ohio State offseason, emerging as a true freshman capable of starting for defensive coordinator Matt Patricia. He impressed in spring practice drills, worked his way up the depth chart in preseason camp and solidified himself as the Buckeyes’ top nickelback by Week 1. His performance in Saturday’s 19-15 win at Indiana was a reminder of how Timmons’ rise was possible. The former five-star prospect is a playmaker — one that has shown up for Ohio State in the biggest moments, even as Timmons has battled injury. The Hoosiers learned that, when healthy, he’s among the Buckeyes’ most dangerous defensive players. Indiana opened the second half with its offense on the field, trailing 10-7 after losing momentum late in the first half. Quarterback Josh Hoover seemed to have his team trending back in the right direction, though, with a 19-yard completion to Davion Chandler on the second play from scrimmage in the half. The Buckeyes only managed to score three points on the ensuing drive, giving the Hoosiers a chance to move past the fumble. They started strong, with Hoover finding star receiver Charlie Becker for a 36-yard completion. Timmons, again, prevented Indiana from finding further success. On the first-down play following Becker’s catch, Indiana threw a screen pass to Tyler Morris. He seemed to have an open field ahead of him, only needing to get past a freshman defensive back. Timmons won the battle, taking down Morris for no gain. He added a pass breakup on second down and a tackle short of the line to gain on third. While impressive, Timmons’ performance wasn’t surprising. He played 62 defensive snaps in Ohio State’s Week 2 loss at Texas — the first ranked matchup of the freshman’s career. He forced a fumble on his first play from scrimmage and delivered a big hit on quarterback Arch Manning later in the contest. Timmons remained a regular part of Ohio State’s defense in the weeks that followed, but an injury late in a Sept. 26 win against Illinois sidetracked his season. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland — contests that saw Ohio State’s defense take a step forward after a shaky first quarter of the regular season. Coming off two straight blowouts, the Gators should come out with urgency, and an offense that ranks 8th in EPA per pass can keep them close for a half. Texas's offense isn't built to jump out to fast leads either. The second half is where the Longhorns' advantages show up. Coming off a loss, Texas is eager to get back in the conference title picture with a good showing against the reeling Gators. Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. Pass protection has been mixed despite solid grades in some metrics, and the run game has lacked consistent explosiveness. Where Texas separates itself is on defense. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. Rushing off the edges and overall tackling efficiency have been strengths. That could create some real problems for a Florida offense that has looked worn down. Defensive collapse, run game issues at Florida NCAA Football: Mississippi at Florida Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Even during the Gators' win streak, critics sounded the alarm about this defense. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. picks.headline: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome
picks.blurb: Gators Legend Chris Doering Predicts 'Nasty' Gators vs. No. 7 Longhorns Outcome - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball sign up 49ers keep rolling Rays heading to World Series Reese, Dream get even Hurts reportedly out for season For the Gators to upset Texas, they're going to need a big day from running back Jadan Baugh. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Scott Kennedy Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:41 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators take on the No. 7 Texas Longhorns on Saturday at Noon EST . The Gators will be eager to return to the field after a pair of less-than-stellar performances the last two weeks. Head coach Jon Sumrall admitted earlier this week that he was taking a more hands-on approach to making sure his players understood what it meant to play Florida Gators football. They'll also be giving second-year quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. his first start after seeing mop-up duty the last two weeks. Gators legend Chris Doering appeared on the Paul Finebaum show to preview the Gators at Longhorns, and he was having flashbacks from the last time Florida traveled to Austin. "For whatever reason, I cannot get the idea or the memory of watching Scott Strickland on the sideline two years ago, last time that Florida went to Austin, and I think they were down 42-0 in the first half and 11:00 a.m. (Central) start," Doering said on the show . Doering was off by a touchdown. It was 35-0 en route to a 49-17 Texas win. However, the kickoff time isn't the only similarity Doering points out. Florida started a backup quarterback two years ago as well. "They were without their starting quarterback. Maybe his mobility can help going up against probably the best front seven that they will face the entire season," Doering said of Jones. Sumrall was unhappy with how the Gators played on the lines of scrimmage in their two losses, and Doering is afraid that won't be fixed quickly enough to beat a powerful Longhorns team. "The blueprint's out on beating Florida. It's being able to out-physical them on the line of scrimmage, being able to stop the run. Everything starts with the run game for Florida. Then the secondary is incredibly porous. Something that we were afraid of in the offseason is now coming to light. "Teams are being able to take advantage of it the last couple of weeks, including last week with LaNorris Sellers converted, I think, about five or six 3rd and 10 pluses." Sellers was an incredibly efficient 23 of 35 passing for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Gamecocks' 38-19 win. They were 10 for 16 overall on third down. Texas managed 382 yards against Oklahoma last week, but they only scored 24 points in the 27-24 loss to the Sooners. Tennessee held them to 262 yards and 20 points in the previous game. Doering thinks this could be the week the Longhorn offense breaks out. "So, I feel like Texas, if you ever wanted a slump buster, this is it for Texas's offense. I think it's going to get nasty, unfortunately, there in Austin. I think Texas wins by multiple touchdowns," Doering finished. The Longhorns present a big challenge to the Gators, but that also means it's a big opportunity to get back into the College Football Playoff conversation with an upset. Except for one touchdown drive, Texas quarterback Arch Manning and the Longhorns offense were totally dominated late in the game. The UT defense, who were hung out to dry by the offense, struggled to stop the short yardage offense of Florida. Backup QB Tramell Jones Jr. was able to get the ball out quickly, utilizing a short passing game that got the ball to his wide receivers before the typically stout Texas defensive line could collapse the pocket. Jones was also able to run the ball effectively when called upon. Jones ran for 41 yards on 10 carries. To make matters worse, the best player on this Texas team might be out for an extended amount of time. All-American EDGE Colin Simmons left the game with an apparent knee injury and did not return, eventually being taken to the locker room on a golf cart. Check out the complete details of Texas' collapse below: It doesn't look like Texas EDGE Colin Simmons will return. Simmons suffered an apparent knee injury earlier in the fourth quarter and has now been taken to the locker room on a golf cart. After a three and out from the Texas offense, the Gators got the ball with a chance to take the lead. But UT EDGE Colin Simmons sacked Florida QB Tramell Jones Jr. to force a punt. After scoring on their first two drives, the Longhorns offense has struggled on the last two. A three-and-out by Texas gives the Gators the ball with good field position. Florida goes three and out on first possession The Longhorns defense forced a three and out on the Gators first offensive possession. Sophomore QB Tramell Jones Jr. hit TE Luke Harpring for a five-yard pass on third down, but he was just short of a first down. Deep in its own territory, Florida elected to punt, The Florida Gators will reportedly start backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. against Texas today. Starting Gators QB Aaron Philo will be a game-time decision. Philo has been limited all week by a shoulder injury he suffered against South Carolina last Saturday in a 38-19 loss to the Gamecocks. This will be the first career start for Jones, who took most of the first team reps this week in practice. Texas defensive lineman Justus Terry and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, both listed as probable all week, are not on today's report meaning they should be good to go. Defensively, Texas has another big day. Florida QB Aaron Philo is questionable, as are WRs Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton. The Gators will get some yards on the ground with super running back Jadan Baugh. But the passing game will be a mess. Texas defensive lineman Justus Terry is listed as probable. Terry has missed the past four games after suffering a toe/foot injury in warmups for the Ohio State game. He suited up last week for the Oklahoma game, but did not play. Presumably, Terry was dressed if needed in an emergency, similar to Hollywood Smothers against Tennessee. Jordan Coleman is also probable. Offensive line

away.headline: Florida injury report: Philo, Brown, Stockton game-time decisions
away.blurb: Running back Duke Clark remains out and will not be available to play. Quarterback Aaron Philo and wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton are all listed as game-time decisions ahead of the noon ET kickoff. Philo's status has been one of the biggest questions of the week. CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reported Wednesday that he had been limited in practice as he recovered from a shoulder injury. Presumably, it occurred on a fourth-quarter scramble against South Carolina last Saturday, after which he was pulled for a play and eventually the game. Stockton's appearance on the availability report is for an undisclosed reason, but he recently sustained a back injury on a targeted hit against Ole Miss. He was listed as questionable ahead of the Missouri game but ended up playing in that road loss as well as the homecoming defeat against South Carolina. Texas has two players listed on the final report, with wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman both ruled out. Defensive lineman Justus Terry and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, who appeared on earlier versions of the report, are no longer listed. QB Aaron Philo – game-time decision WR Vernell Brown III – game-time decision WR Bailey Stockton – game-time decision Questionable (50% chance to play) Clark suffered a left ankle injury in the first half against South Carolina last Saturday and wore a boot on the sideline in the second half. His injury will likely take multiple weeks to heal. On3's Pete Nakos reported Friday that Florida is expected to start Tramell Jones against Texas, although a final determination on the quarterback situation was expected Saturday morning. Brown's absence would continue a lengthy stretch on the sideline after he sustained a knee strain against Ole Miss in Week 4. The sophomore standout missed most of that game and both of the past two contests against Missouri and South Carolina. "VB's trying to play. He's not like, 'I'm going to take the week off' or 'I'm going to take next week.' No, he's trying like hell to play," Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said Monday. "But at the same time, we have to be smart-tough, not dumb-tough." away.headline: Final injury report for Texas Longhorns vs. Florida Gators in Week 7
away.blurb: As the Horns flew toward their Week 7 matchup against the Florida Gators, their injury report was as short as it had been all season, and that included the return of defensive lineman Justus Terry and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman to the availability list. However, the Gators were counting down the seconds until they had to make a few game-time decisions that could make or break their chance to keep pace with No. 7 Texas. So, with less than an hour until kickoff, which players are in, which ones are out, and which ones' availabilities could come down to the last possible moment? OUT: Kaliq Lockett, wide receiver; Jaydon Chatman, offensive lineman GAME-TIME DECISION: Aaron Philo, quarterback; Bailey Stockton, wide receiver; Vernell Brown III, wide receiver Additionally, Florida may be without two of its top three wide receivers, with both Bailey Stockton and Vernell Brown III listed as "game-time decisions," just like their quarterback. Running back Duke Clark was the only Gator listed as officially "out" on the final availability report. Final injury report for Texas Longhorns vs. Florida Gators in Week 7 Skip to main content Recruiting Over the last three weeks, the Texas Longhorns and head coach Steve Sarkisian seem to have placed a renewed emphasis on getting the team as healthy as possible. No. 7 Texas Longhorns availability report for Week 7 vs. Florida IN: Justus Terry, defensive lineman; Jordan Coleman, offensive lineman While the Texas offensive line will have renewed depth with Coleman returning to the possible rotation, it will also be without Jaydon Chatman. However, Chatman, who is a fourth-year OL who has appeared in just 19 games, isn't a starter for the Horns, so it isn't a massive loss on the depth chart. Similarly, wideout Kaliq Lockett, a second-year receiver, has appeared in two games so far this season, but has recorded just one reception for a three-yard loss. Unsurprisingly, the young wide receiver is not part of the starting rotation. Florida Gators availability report for Week 7 vs. Texas With a seemingly opposite availability report, the Gators could be without three of their star offensive players, including starting quarterback Aaron Philo. A couple of hours before kickoff, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that the Gators had officially decided to start backup QB Tramell Jones Jr., who has just 64 career pass attempts. However, it looks like Philo could possibly rotate in if things start to go south. Going up against the T exas defense is already a tall task for any team , much less a group that's on a two-game losing streak and could very well be without three offensive stars. The No. 7 Texas Longhorns (4-1 overall, 1-1 SEC) and the unranked Florida Gators (4-2 overall, 2-2 SEC) are scheduled to kick off at 11 a.m. CT on Saturday, Sept. 17, and the game will be broadcast on ABC.

home.headline: Texas football’s Colin Simmons injury update delivers another blow amid Arch Manning mess
home.blurb: Texas football has not played well over the past two weeks, and there’s a good chance that Arch Manning will be benched as KJ Lacey Jr. is expected to take some first-team reps this week. That’s not the only big news coming out of Texas, with Colin Simmons leaving the game against Florida with an injury, and his status is in doubt for next week, according to Pete Nakos of On3. As much as Simmons’ injury is a serious topic, everyone is still looking at the Manning situation in shock. He was slated to be one of the top quarterbacks going into the draft next year, and if he actually gets benched, his stock could take a big hit. There could even be a scenario where he decides to return to Texas for another year. Related: Florida State’s Mike Norvell is now calling out ‘absolute joke’ of a call that ruined Hail Mary TD vs. Miami “Texas star EDGE Colin Simmons sustained an ankle sprain in Saturday’s loss to Florida, sources tell On3. His status for this week against Ole Miss is in question. He leads the nation with 10.5 sacks,” Nakos wrote on X, formerly Twitter. That’s not the best news for Texas, and all eyes will be on them this week to see if Simmons suits up for practice at any point. If not, it might be safe to say that they’ll be playing without him, and that means it’s next man up on the defensive line. There is still a lot of the season left, so Manning has some time to fix what he needs to, but it looks like head coach Steve Sarkisian has him on a short leash. Like ClutchPoints’ content? home.headline: One Texas player upgraded on Thursday injury report
home.blurb: Another Longhorns player was ruled out against the Gators. The second injury report is out ahead of Saturday’s matchup between the No. 7 Texas Longhorns and the Florida Gators at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium with one player upgraded and one player downgraded for head coach Steve Sarkisian’s team. Sophomore wide receiver Kaliq Lockett was downgraded from questionable to out, joining senior offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman, who was ruled out on Thursday. Sophomore offensive lineman Jordan Coleman, however, was upgraded from questionable to probable, joining sophomore defensive lineman Justus Terry, who was still listed as probable on Thursday. There were no changes to Florida’s injury report with quarterback Aaron Philo and wide receivers Vernell Brown III and wide receiver Bailey Stockton still listed as questionable. Philo sustained a shoulder injury in last Saturday’s loss to South Carolina, while Brown hasn’t played since the win over Ole Miss. According to ESPN , all three players are expected to be game-time decisions. picks.headline: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why?
picks.blurb: LSU vs. Mississippi State Final Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB After LSU traveled to Lexington last weekend, Lane Kiffin and the Tigers are coming off of a disappointing loss, heading into the Week 7 matchup against Mississippi State . LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Oct 3, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers safety Tamarcus Cooley (0) intercepts a pass from McNeese Cowboys quarterback Jake Strong (not pictured) during the first half at Tiger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. LSU 44, Mississippi State 21 Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Adrian Ramirez Adrian Ramirez LSU will bounce back from its overtime loss to Kentucky with a strong performance at home in Tiger Stadium. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. LSU 35, Mississippi State 21 Published Oct 16, 2026 BROOKE BENEDICT Brooke Benedict is a sophomore at LSU, majoring in journalism. She is originally from Boulder, Colorado, and enjoys skiing, hiking, and Pilates. She's always enjoyed watching sports and the way sports bring people together. She has spent one semester as a sports columnist for the LSU student newspaper, and is am excited to continue her LSU sports reporting career with On SI. No. 22 LSU welcomes No. 16 Mississippi State to Baton Rouge on Saturday, with the Tigers laying 14.5 points despite the Bulldogs entering as the higher-ranked team. My Mississippi State vs. LSU prediction backs the Tigers' defense to dictate the tempo against a Bulldogs offense dealing with uncertainty at quarterback. Mississippi State standout Kamario Taylor is questionable with a foot injury, and LSU has the defensive personnel to make life difficult regardless of who starts under center. Read on for my analysis and more college football picks for Saturday, Oct. 17. TOP PICK Who will win Mississippi State vs LSU: LSU -14.5 I'll play LSU at -14.5 to 55%. Although Mississippi State has one of the best offenses in the country, ranking fifth in adjusted EPA per play, that production runs through quarterback Kamario Taylor . He's questionable with a foot injury that clearly limited him against Alabama, while leading rusher Fluff Bothwell is also questionable. Even a fully healthy Bulldogs attack would be in for a fight. LSU's defense ranks fourth in adjusted EPA per play and fourth in EPA per pass allowed (-0.26) . Despite a lacklustre performance against Kentucky last weekend, I'm still a believer in this Tigers unit because of those metrics. On the other side, Mississippi State's defense is 101st in success rate allowed and 99th against the pass , giving inconsistent QB Sam Leavitt plenty of room to work, even with his mistakes. But Lane Kiffin's bunch lost to Ole Miss, came back with a few wins, and then last week got outfoxed by Kentucky in a 35-34 overtime loss. And now there's a problem. LSU is talented enough to beat anyone, but it's one more loss away from realistically being out of the College Football Playoff. That won't be easy with a brutal schedule over the second half of the season. Mississippi State has had two weeks to get over the 56-23 loss to Alabama. It isn't an easy slate, but at 4-1, it'll still be in the mix for big things if it can get out of Baton Rouge with a win. Mississippi State vs LSU: Quick Hits LSU starts a run of three home games in the next four weeks, going to Auburn next before hosting Alabama and Texas. Mississippi State starts its own run of four home games in five weeks after this, hosting Oklahoma before going to Texas. LSU has won three straight in the series ever since the 44-34 loss to open up the 2020 season. That came right after the Tigers' national title season. The Bulldogs have been winning on their amazing offense, but the defense has held its own in key spots. It might be tough to hang with the Tigers blow for blow, so taking the ball away is a must. Mississippi State came up with two takeaways in two of the last three games, and turnovers have been a big issue for LSU, with ten in six games. Why does the defense have to come up big? Why LSU Will Win Mississippi State might be without star quarterback Kamario Taylor. He's trying to get past a leg injury suffered in the Alabama loss, and now he and top running back Fluff Bothwell are questionable at best. There's also the home-field advantage side of this. Ole Miss and Kentucky are good, but LSU should've been better in both road games. At home, the Tigers have been untouchable, winning by a combined score of 194-44 in the four games. Mississippi State vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It'll be a different LSU team than the one that walked off the field against Kentucky. It'll be more confident, explosive, and it won't let up – this won't be a back-and-forth fight like it was against the Wildcats. Of course, this changes if Taylor is at 100% for the Bulldogs, but even if he's ready to roll, LSU will be razor-sharp with a much better defensive performance than last week. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. away.blurb: With Taylor ruled out against LSU, redshirt freshman walk-on Billy Puckett received his first career start. Puckett finished 16-of-26 for 121 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception. STARKVILLE — Mississippi State football desperately needed a spark against LSU on Saturday, but could a healthy Kamario Taylor have made the difference? The Bulldogs suffered a crushing 31-0 defeat in Baton Rouge, recording their first shutout since 2020. Without Taylor and leading running back Fluff Bothwell, Mississippi State struggled to generate offense against an LSU defense that consistently pressured the quarterback and forced the Bulldogs into difficult situations. Taylor’s absence undoubtedly hurt. However, even if the breakout quarterback had been healthy enough to play, Mississippi State still would have faced a difficult challenge against the Tigers. Taylor’s Absence Left Mississippi State Without Its Biggest Weapon Taylor entered the LSU matchup as one of college football’s breakout stars, recording 1,450 passing yards, 159 rushing yards and 18 total touchdowns through five games. His production helped Mississippi State win its first four games of the season for the first time since 2014. His ability to make plays with his arm and legs gave the Bulldogs an offensive dimension they struggled to replicate against LSU. Unfortunately, Taylor was still recovering from a foot injury suffered against Missouri on September 26. He played through the injury against Alabama two weeks earlier, but visible discomfort, two interceptions and five sacks highlighted how difficult it was for him to operate at full strength. He eventually left that game in the third quarter. Although Puckett showed composure in challenging circumstances, Mississippi State lacked the explosive playmaking that had made its offense dangerous earlier in the season. STARKVILLE — Mississippi State football desperately needed a spark against LSU on Saturday, but could a healthy Kamario Taylor have made the difference? The Bulldogs suffered a crushing 31-0 defeat in Baton Rouge, recording their first shutout since 2020. Without Taylor and leading running back Fluff Bothwell, Mississippi State struggled to generate offense against an LSU defense that consistently pressured the quarterback and forced the Bulldogs into difficult situations. Taylor’s absence undoubtedly hurt. However, even if the breakout quarterback had been healthy enough to play, Mississippi State still would have faced a difficult challenge against the Tigers. Taylor’s Absence Left Mississippi State Without Its Biggest Weapon Taylor entered the LSU matchup as one of college football’s breakout stars, recording 1,450 passing yards, 159 rushing yards and 18 total touchdowns through five games. His production helped Mississippi State win its first four games of the season for the first time since 2014. His ability to make plays with his arm and legs gave the Bulldogs an offensive dimension they struggled to replicate against LSU. Unfortunately, Taylor was still recovering from a foot injury suffered against Missouri on September 26. He played through the injury against Alabama two weeks earlier, but visible discomfort, two interceptions and five sacks highlighted how difficult it was for him to operate at full strength. He eventually left that game in the third quarter. Although Puckett showed composure in challenging circumstances, Mississippi State lacked the explosive playmaking that had made its offense dangerous earlier in the season. LSU controlled the game , and the Bulldogs struggled in several critical areas beyond the quarterback position. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. How To Watch Auburn vs Georgia Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Auburn Will Win The Auburn defense has been great. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. The Georgia Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn is a team that's trying to turn their program around. And, Alex Golesh is looking for that first unranked-upset win over a rival. Can he get it done on Saturday? A to Z Sports' experts picked the final scores for this game. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. Their win over Alabama is about as good as it gets for any team this season, other than maybe Texas beating Ohio State. But, they have to show they can be consistent. And, there are definitely still things to work on. As for Auburn, this offense has not been as fun to watch as we all maybe thought it would in the offseason. But Georgia has the mix of defense and offense that Auburn just simply won't be able to hang around with. Then again, this is a rivalry game, and we've seen some weird things happen in rivalry games this year alone. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.blurb: Per the SEC’s Availability Report, Nate Frazier is expected to be available for Georgia’s game against Auburn on Saturday, but junior safety KJ Bolden is questionable. Georgia has already ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion, sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear, junior running back Chauncey Bowens, junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green. Junior offensive lineman Marcus Harrison, who has missed the past four games, is considered probable. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since.

home.headline: Georgia football injury report: Key Georgia defender questionable for Auburn
home.blurb: Per the SEC’s Availability Report, Nate Frazier is expected to be available for Georgia’s game against Auburn on Saturday, but junior safety KJ Bolden is questionable. He’s one of six Bulldogs listed on the report , which was released Wednesday night. Georgia has already ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion, sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear, junior running back Chauncey Bowens, junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green. Junior offensive lineman Marcus Harrison, who has missed the past four games, is considered probable. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since.

home.headline: SEC Availability Report | Georgia's KJ Bolden downgraded to out for Auburn
home.blurb: Safety KJ Bolden, the star junior, is now listed as out. He was downgraded from questionable to doubtful on Thursday and then out on Friday. Wide receiver Isiah Canion and running back Chauncey Bowens are listed as out. Offensive lineman Marcus Harrison went from probable to not listed, meaning he's available to play. These Georgia players are listed as out These Georgia players are listed as doubtful These Georgia players are listed as questionable These Georgia players are listed as probable Auburn: OUT: Offensive lineman Tai Buster (undisclosed), TE Hunter Herring (undisclosed), LB Xavier Atkins (non-injury related). Georgia has six players listed on the latest report, updated most recently on Saturday, Oct. 17. Bolden was helped to the sideline with an apparent leg injury after his third-down sack late in the win at Alabama but appeared Monday for his normal WSB interview. He was wearing a sleeve on the right leg during the interview. Bolden is fourth on the Bulldogs with 22 tackles and has one interception and two pass breakups. Running back Nate Frazier, who warmed up but did not play against Alabama due to a lingering rib injury, again is not on the availability report just like last week. Canion has missed the last three games with what coach Kirby Smart Monday called a "lower extremity injury." Bowens sustained a lower body injury in the win against Vanderbilt two weeks ago and did not play at Alabama. This is the third season that the conference has had reporting policies for schools ahead of SEC games. home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season As it turns out though, Kirby Smart's team is going to be a little bit banged up as they try to avoid a first home defeat against Auburn in more than two decades. As was the case last week, the running back room is going to be a bit thin. With the reporting around Chauncey Bowens as murky as ever, he has been ruled out for the second straight week and could wind up missing more time than that. Bowens is ruled out along with Isiah Canion, who has not seen much work this season. Thomas Blackshear is also out once again, but this is not a huge surprise. The bigger surprising thing is KJ Bolden being listed as questionable, potentially banged up from the Alabama game but dealing with an unknown injury. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Alabama looks to recover from its first loss of the season on Saturday at No. 14 Tennessee Getty Images Two longtime SEC rivals with playoff aspirations are squaring off in a top-15 showdown on Saturday, as No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee on the traditional Third Saturday in October. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Where to watch Alabama vs. Tennessee live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Neyland Stadium -- Knoxville, Tennessee TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Alabama vs. Tennessee prediction, picks Tennessee's defense and run game have carried it to a 5-1 start. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. This game features a quarterback reunion as former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons returns to Oxford. It should be a highly competitive matchup with massive stakes. Here are three bold Ole Miss predictions for Saturday's game. Kewan Lacy Goes Over 100 Rushing Yards Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kewan Lacy returned to the lineup after a one-game absence against Florida and finished with seven carries for 39 yards.
